title: DR1 has the user add transit countries one at a time by searching, and lists what they added with a Remove link beside each; the frontend offers a flat list of 31 checkboxes, so the order the consignment passes through is never recorded.

finding.frontend: Under the label "Select all countries the consignment will travel through" the page renders every country as a checkbox in one alphabetical column, thirty-one of them from Austria to Switzerland, and the user scrolls and ticks (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js:22-27). What is stored is a set, deduplicated and unordered (:61-65). There is no search, nothing shows back which countries have been chosen apart from the ticks themselves, and there is nothing to remove — a user un-ticks. Nothing anywhere records that the consignment passes through France before Belgium.
finding.prototype: The page asks "Enter a country", hinted "Enter each country that the consignment will travel through", over a single search box placeholdered "Search for a country" (app/views/transit-countries.html:56-115). Each country the user picks is appended to a list below headed "Country", one row each, with a "Remove" link on the right. The list keeps the order they were added in, and the review page prints them in that order.
finding.difference: Replace the checkbox list with a country search that appends to a growing, removable list, and store the answer as an ordered sequence rather than a set. This changes what the answer means as well as how it is collected, so the stored shape and anything that reads it — the hub, the review page, the submitted payload — has to accept an ordered list. It travels with the two findings about the rules the frontend puts on this field, since all three change the same control.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a search input or a remove control on fe-transit-countries — the captured DOM for that screen is one checkbox group and the Save buttons.
